paras: The lynching of Rupe was the killing by a mob of a man named Rupe at Tomlinson, Arkansas, after he shot a man named Fuller, an event reported in early March 1881. It is known only from a one-sentence news brief, which said the townspeople found the shooting "despicable" and that "A mob murdered the murderer." The same paragraph circulated as filler in Pennsylvania, Illinois and Ohio papers between March and April 1881.

According to the brief, Rupe shot Fuller while Fuller "was at the moment proffering his hand in token of his desire to be friendly." The people of Tomlinson, the item said, considered the shooting "despicable" for that reason. It called Rupe "the murderer," which implies that Fuller died of the wound, and closed by stating that a mob had killed him.
The paragraph gives no date, county, first names or races for either man. Nor does it say how large the mob was, whether Rupe had been arrested, or where and how he was killed.
No report of an arrest, inquest or prosecution of anyone in the mob appears in the coverage.

The item first appears in The Post of Middleburg, Pennsylvania, on March 3, 1881, in a column of short state and national notes, between an item on a Boston printing-house fire and a line about Senator Fair. The Daily Cairo Bulletin of Cairo, Illinois, printed it word for word under "News Brevities" on March 23, and the Democratic Press of Ravenna, Ohio, ran the same column, with the same neighboring item on a Marysville, Ohio, divorce, on April 7. The identical wording across these papers points to a single circulated paragraph rather than separate reports, and no Arkansas account was found.

The brief made no reference to race and offered no endorsement of the mob, applying the word "murdered" to the mob's act even as it labeled Rupe a murderer. One machine reading of the Post prints the shooter's name as "Rape," while the other copies read "Rupe."
